root_cause.text: The xe driver fails to re-evaluate display presence after `intel_display_device_info_runtime_init()` may disable display via fuses, leaving `xe->info.probe_display` incorrectly set to true, which later causes display code to operate on uninitialized mode config and trigger a NULL pointer dereference.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check for `intel_display_device_present()` after `intel_display_device_info_runtime_init()`, and resets `xe->info.probe_display = false` and calls `unset_display_features()` if display is not present. The CVE description confirms that the oops occurs in `xe_display_flush_cleanup_work()` when iterating over CRTCs via `for_each_intel_crtc()` on uninitialized mode config.

The CVE description confirms that the oops occurs in `xe_display_flush_cleanup_work()` when iterating over CRTCs via `for_each_intel_crtc()` on uninitialized mode config.

Function that may disable display via fuses, but its result is not checked to update probe_display flag.
Directly causes NULL pointer dereference when display is disabled but probe_display is still true, operating on uninitialized mode config.

Error handling jump that does not re-evaluate display presence, leaving probe_display mis-set.

Part of initialization sequence that sets up display state early, but does not account for later fusing that may disable display, contributing to the incorrect probe_display assumption.
Registers opregion before runtime_init; while not directly causing the NULL dereference, it is part of the path that assumes display is present and remains called even if display is later disabled.
Initializes bandwidth hardware before runtime_init; though not directly responsible, it is part of the initialization sequence that operates under the assumption that display is present.
